questions.question: What is the keyboard shortcut to run your Python code?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Enter (or Cmd+Enter on Mac) is the primary shortcut for running code. This allows you to test your program without taking your hands off the keyboard.

questions.question: How do you quickly comment or uncomment multiple lines of code?
options: Select the lines and press Ctrl+/ (Cmd+/ on Mac)
Type # at the beginning of each line manually
Use the Format button in the editor
questions.explanation: Select the lines you want to comment/uncomment and press Ctrl+/ (Cmd+/ on Mac). This toggles Python comments (#) on all selected lines, saving you from manually editing each line.

questions.question: What does Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click on Mac) do in the editor?
options: Adds another cursor at the clicked position
Jumps to the definition of a function
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click on Mac) adds multiple cursors at each clicked position. This powerful feature lets you edit the same text in multiple places simultaneously.

questions.question: How can you quickly clear the terminal output?
options: Close and reopen the browser tab
Press Ctrl+L (Cmd+L on Mac) or click the Clear button
Wait for it to automatically clear after 5 minutes
questions.explanation: Ctrl+L (Cmd+L on Mac) or the Clear button instantly clears all terminal output. This is useful when you want a fresh workspace without old results cluttering the view.
